## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Add coverage for adopting an existing setting whose value already matches the incoming value, the case that distinguishes adoption from replacement.

## Changes
The settings merger gains an `adopt` flag that assigns incoming values to existing keys and records those keys in the change list. The merger writes the configuration whenever that list contains entries.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/config.py:13 — tests — Cover adoption when the value already matches — With `adopt=True` and both values set to `theme="dark"`, the merger records `theme` and writes the file, but the adoption test only covers a value change. — A regression that skips matching keys during adoption could pass the suite and leave callers without the expected adoption record.

## Suggestions
- app/config.py:18 — tests — Cover existing settings with both flags off — When the stored theme is `light` and the incoming theme is `dark`, the default merge skips the existing key, but the default-mode test only covers inserting a new key. — An accidental overwrite of an existing setting in default mode could pass the suite.
